title: Leadership in AI Assisted Engineering – Justin Reock, DX (acq. Atlassian)
talk_summary: A leadership/management talk about AI-assisted engineering adoption, arguing that averages hide huge per-company variance and that outcomes depend on education, psychological safety, and measuring speed+quality rather than utilization. It offers few agent-system mechanisms, but a handful of concrete practices (system-prompt feedback gatekeeping, temperature control, bottleneck targeting, context injection for incidents) are copyable.

takeaways.technique: System-prompt/agent-rules feedback loop with a gatekeeper
takeaways.what_they_do: Route recurring model mistakes (e.g. outdated framework versions) into a maintained rules file, owned by a designated group that continuously improves the system prompts/agent markdown.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Have a gatekeeper... a group in the organization that can receive this feedback that understand how to maintain and continuously improve these system prompts

takeaways.technique: Temperature as a per-task determinism dial
takeaways.what_they_do: Set low temperature (~0.001) for tasks needing reproducible output and higher (~0.9) only where divergent approaches are wanted; avoid exactly 0 or 1.
takeaways.evidence_quote: When we have a lower temperature... 0.001, we give it the same task twice, and it gives us the exact same output character for character

takeaways.technique: Fix the actual bottleneck, not the easy step
takeaways.what_they_do: Apply theory of constraints: time saved on a non-bottleneck is worthless; identify where the queue actually is and target AI there.
takeaways.evidence_quote: An hour saved on something that isn't the bottleneck is worthless. And when we look at data... there are definitely good... time savings with AI that are being eclipsed by sources of context switching

takeaways.technique: Auto-inject runbook + incident context into the responder channel
takeaways.what_they_do: On incident detection, pull runbook steps and relevant docs and push them into the responder channel so responders skip the context-gathering minutes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: taking things like run but steps and and other areas of context and documentation and pushing them directly into S sur channels... they just eliminated that time

takeaways.what_they_do: Track AI utilization alongside outcome metrics like change failure rate, change confidence, and maintainability; utilization alone doesn't tell you if it's working.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Our AI metrics like utilization and things are telling us what's happening with the tech, but these core metrics... are telling us whether these initiatives are actually working
takeaways.numbers: industry benchmark change failure rate ~4%; some orgs saw up to 50% more defects

takeaways.what_they_do: Add fields to the PR form (e.g. 'AI-generated?') to get ground-truth signal that API telemetry can't provide.
takeaways.evidence_quote: add a new field to a PR form that says I used AI to generate this PR... and get some data that way
